name: Order supplies
description: Par levels and a reorder point that a purchasing bot or a spreadsheet can order from, for about 200 drinks a day: beans 31 kg weekly with a top-up when 10.5 kg are left, whole milk 50 L per every-other-day delivery, oat milk 68 L and 950 takeaway cups weekly, keeping stock value under $1,300 so nothing runs out and nothing spoils.

learned_parameters.label: Beans
learned_parameters.rationale: Set to 31 kg. In attempt #1, 24 kg failed (score 24.3, beans sub-score 22), causing the grinder to run dry on Saturday. In attempt #4, 28 kg scored 94.6 (sub-score 75) with Saturday stockouts. A setting of 31 kg achieved a 100 sub-score across attempts #2, #3, #5, #6, #7, #8, #9, and #10, aligning with resting and roasting freshness cycles. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 31 kg. Tried 24 kg (sub-score 22) to 31 kg (sub-score 100). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 31 kg and 31 kg. Too low (28 kg): "Ran out of espresso beans on Saturday: the grinder ran dry mid-rush."

learned_parameters.label: Reorder beans at
learned_parameters.rationale: Set to 10.5 kg. In attempt #1, 6 kg failed (sub-score 8) because the delivery van arrived too late. In attempt #2, 10 kg yielded a sub-score of 97. Raising to 10.5 kg achieved a perfect 100 sub-score and overall score 100.0 in attempt #3 (also tested at 11 kg and 12 kg in attempts #5 and #6 yielding 100), fulfilling safety buffer requirements as described in bar reorder point literature. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 11 kg. Keep 10.5 kg: with it the total score was best (100.0), because the relation terms depend on it too. Tried 6 kg (sub-score 8) to 12 kg (sub-score 100). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 10 kg and 12 kg.

learned_parameters.label: Milk per delivery
learned_parameters.rationale: Set to 50 L per delivery. In attempt #1, 36 L failed (score 24.3, sub-score 14) running out by Thursday lunch. In attempt #7, 56 L resulted in 12 L going sour (score 93.9, sub-score 73). In attempt #8, reducing to 44 L scored 98.3 (sub-score 92). A batch size of 50 L achieved a perfect 100 sub-score in attempts #2, #3, #5, #6, #9, and #10, strictly respecting dairy shelf-life limits. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 50 L. Tried 36 L (sub-score 14) to 56 L (sub-score 73). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 44 L and 50 L. Too high (56 L): "12 L of milk went sour in the fridge before anyone could use it."

learned_parameters.label: Oat milk
learned_parameters.rationale: Set to 68 L. In attempt #1, 50 L scored 24.3 (sub-score 8) due to severe shortages. Setting to 68 L achieved a 100 sub-score in all subsequent attempts (#2 through #10), satisfying weekly volume while adhering to the standard 5-day post-opening shelf life. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 68 L. Tried 50 L (sub-score 8) to 68 L (sub-score 100). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 68 L and 68 L.

learned_parameters.label: Paper cups
learned_parameters.rationale: Set to 950 cups. In attempt #1, 700 cups scored 24.3 (sub-score 25) due to stockout risk. Increasing to 950 cups achieved a 100 sub-score across attempts #2 through #10 without incurring excessive holding costs. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 950 cups. Tried 700 cups (sub-score 25) to 950 cups (sub-score 100). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 950 cups and 950 cups.

control_effects.effect: Under-ordering at 24 kg (attempt #1) or 28 kg (attempt #4) leads to mid-rush espresso bean depletion on Saturday; 31 kg provides complete weekly coverage with a 100 sub-score. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 31 kg. Tried 24 kg (sub-score 22) to 31 kg (sub-score 100). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 31 kg and 31 kg. Too low (28 kg): "Ran out of espresso beans on Saturday: the grinder ran dry mid-rush."

Setting the reorder point to 6 kg (attempt #1) results in roaster delivery arriving after hoppers empty; 10.0 kg (attempt #2) reaches 97 sub-score; 10.5 kg to 12.0 kg (attempts #3, #5, #6, #9, #10) reaches 100 sub-score. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 11 kg. Keep 10.5 kg: with it the total score was best (100.0), because the relation terms depend on it too. Tried 6 kg (sub-score 8) to 12 kg (sub-score 100). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 10 kg and 12 kg.

Under-ordering at 36 L (attempt #1) causes lattes to drop off the menu Thursday; 44 L (attempt #8) scores 92; 56 L (attempt #7) results in 12 L of sour spoilage; exactly 50 L yields a 100 sub-score. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 50 L. Tried 36 L (sub-score 14) to 56 L (sub-score 73). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 44 L and 50 L. Too high (56 L): "12 L of milk went sour in the fridge before anyone could use it."

Increasing from 50 L (attempt #1, sub-score 8) to 68 L (attempts #2-#10) completely avoids alternative milk runouts, scoring 100. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 68 L. Tried 50 L (sub-score 8) to 68 L (sub-score 100). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 68 L and 68 L.

Increasing from 700 cups (attempt #1, sub-score 25) to 950 cups (attempts #2-#10) ensures takeout demand is fully met while keeping cash-on-shelves at 100. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 950 cups. Tried 700 cups (sub-score 25) to 950 cups (sub-score 100). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 950 cups and 950 cups.
Cash on shelves was 100/100 because inventory was low, but at the cost of severe stockouts. Measured: Relation 'Cash on shelves' depends on several controls together; best sub-score 100/100.

steps: Tools: an inventory sheet of on-hand counts, a standing order per supplier (roaster weekly, dairy every 2 days, oat milk and cups weekly) sent by email or supplier API, and a bean reorder trigger at the learned reorder point.
Set weekly espresso bean inventory (beans_kg) to 31 kg.
Set the bean reorder point trigger (beans_rop_kg) to 10.5 kg.
Set the dairy milk delivery batch size (milk_l) to 50 L per delivery.
Set weekly oat milk inventory (oat_l) to 68 L.
Set weekly paper cup stock (cups) to 950 cups.
caveats: Dairy milk has strict shelf-life limitations; ordering above 50 L per delivery leads to sour milk waste.
Dropping beans_kg below 31 kg causes espresso shortages before the end of the week, especially during the Saturday rush.
Setting the beans reorder point at or below 10 kg delays delivery and risks the hopper running dry mid-rush.
Do not drop dairy milk delivery below 50 L (such as 44 L), as it compromises weekly latte supply.
Milk and oat milk spoil if over-ordered too much, so increase systematically rather than maxing out.
All other variables are at perfect 100 sub-scores; do not alter them while fine-tuning the reorder point.
The perfect balance of stock availability and minimal cash on shelves has been found at these exact values.
If you see "Ran out of espresso beans on Saturday: the grinder ran dry mid-rush.", raise Beans.
Keep beans_kg at 31 kg to satisfy weekly customer demand.
Do not adjust milk_l (50), oat_l (68), or cups (950) as they are fully optimized.
Do not drop beans_rop_kg to 10.0 or below as it dips the reorder sub-score below 100.
Do not reduce beans_kg below 31 kg.
Milk per delivery has a tight shelf-life constraint; pushing too far above 50 L risks milk spoilage or reduced cash-on-shelves sub-score.
Keep beans_kg at 31, oat_l at 68, cups at 950, and beans_rop_kg in the 10.5-12.0 range when isolating milk sensitivity.
If you see "12 L of milk went sour in the fridge before anyone could use it.", lower Milk per delivery.
Milk shelf life is strict; delivery quantities above 50 L risk immediate spoilage.
Do not alter beans_kg (31), beans_rop_kg (11.0), oat_l (68), or cups (950) while mapping milk sensitivity.
Milk per delivery has a narrow optimal window around 50 L: below 50 risks shortages and above 50 risks spoilage.
Do not deviate from the known 100.0 configuration (beans_kg: 31, beans_rop_kg: 10.5, milk_l: 50, oat_l: 68, cups: 950).
This is the final attempt; replay the established optimal parameters without any changes.

standing_order.action: order up to par each cycle

reorder_trigger.action: send a bean top-up when on hand <= reorder point

budget_guard.action: block orders that push stock value over the cap

transfer_notes: Par = (usage per cycle + 25% safety) / deliveries and reorder point = daily use x lead time + safety; plug in your own sales and prices and the same rules drive standing orders by email or supplier API.
